unit: episode (title + description with sponsor/ad sentences removed); every guest of the episode gets the episode's labels
purpose: Free, rule-based flag for whether an episode's own RSS text says it is about health or science (code/19_flag_guest_topics.py). Researcher request 2026-10-03, no paid model. Definitions are those of config/content_classification.json; the term lists start from it and are adapted to short RSS text.

labels.health_related: Discussion of physical or mental health, illness, diagnosis, treatment, prevention, sleep, exercise, nutrition, substances, healthcare, or personal health experiences.
labels.science_related: Discussion of scientific research, evidence, studies, experiments, theories, scientific explanations, methods, or scientific institutions.

notes: Measures what the feed text says the episode covers, not what is actually said in the audio.
Terms are matched as whole words, case-insensitive; prefixes match the start of a word.

Dropped from the transcript dictionary because they are ambiguous in titles and ads: 'data', 'study' (alone), 'pain', 'diet' (kept as 'dieting'), 'evidence' (court cases), 'evolution' ('the evolution of comedy'; 'evolutionary' kept), 'universe' ('cinematic universe').

Sentences containing a URL, promo code, discount or sponsor wording are removed before matching (ads for therapy, supplements, telehealth and weight-loss products would otherwise flag almost every episode).
'professor' and 'PhD' were dropped (they do not imply science: professors of law, PhDs in any field); specific field names were added instead.

Guest-level flags use only the title (if it contains the guest's name) and the description sentences that mention the guest's first or last name, plus the sentence after each (descriptions often continue 'They discuss ...').

Phrases in exclude_phrases are removed before matching ('science fiction film' is not science). In titles with several segments ('A on X + B on Y'), only the segments naming the guest count for the guest-level flags.
'treatment' was dropped (film/TV 'treatment', 'memoir treatment'); medical treatment is still caught by the condition or therapy words.

fake_doctors_real_friends_with_zach_and_.reason: Rewatch podcast of the TV hospital comedy 'Scrubs'; medical words describe the fictional show.

small_town_murder.reason: True-crime cases; 'hospital', 'overdose', 'injury' describe crimes, and there are no guests.

boilerplate_rule.description: A sentence (lowercased, letters and digits only) that occurs in at least min_count episodes and at least min_share of a show's episodes is boilerplate (plugs, recurring ads, links) and is removed before matching.
